description: RXRX lottery-call contamination case: raw P/C 0.38 (bullish) inverts to adjusted P/C 2.38 (bearish) after removing 84% lottery volume. Tests whether Critic correctly identifies signal inversion when given BOTH raw and adjusted metrics.

annotations: 84% of call volume is lottery (bid<=0.05, ask<=0.05)
Signal inversion: raw appears bullish, adjusted reveals bearish
7 deep OTM lottery strikes ($5-$11) vs 3 legitimate strikes ($3.50-$4.50)
Put side is clean — no lottery contamination on puts

noise_flags.detail: 84% of call volume comes from contracts priced at $0.01-$0.05. Likely retail lottery activity, not institutional positioning.

annotations: Trading below both 20 and 50 SMA — bearish structure
RSI approaching oversold but not yet at 30

reasoning_steps.examined: Raw P/C ratio of 0.38 suggests strong bullish sentiment
reasoning_steps.conclusion: Surface-level bullish reading is misleading due to lottery contamination

reasoning_steps.examined: 84% lottery volume flag — 154,829 of 184,320 call contracts are penny lottery tickets
reasoning_steps.conclusion: After filtering lottery volume, real call volume is only 29,491 vs 70,042 puts. True P/C is 2.38 — strongly bearish

reasoning_steps.examined: Technical confirmation: price below 20/50 SMA, RSI 38.2
reasoning_steps.conclusion: Technicals align with adjusted (bearish) options signal, not with raw (bullish) reading
Reject bullish thesis. Both adjusted options flow and technicals point bearish. Raw P/C is noise-contaminated and should not inform position sizing.

counter_evidence.claim: RXRX has potential FDA catalyst in June which could explain speculative call buying

outcome.notes: Critic correctly rejected bullish reading. Stock declined 4.8% over the week. Raw signal would have been directionally wrong.
